title: McGuffey's Eclectic Primer
author: William Holmes McGuffey
licenseEvidence: Project Gutenberg eBook #14642: 'Public domain in the USA.' Revised Primer first copyrighted 1881 (Van Antwerp, Bragg & Co.); later renewals 1896 and 1909, all before 1930.
description: The classic first reading book: 52 tiny lessons that add about six new words at a time, from “A cat and a rat” to simple stories and poems. Each day you sound out the new words, read the lesson together, copy a line on a slate or paper, and talk about it. The full text is free online.
includes: 53 short lessons in 10 units (every Primer lesson, plus the closing slate page)
Link to the free full text for every lesson
New words and a sound focus for each lesson
Slate or copywork line and a narration or picture-talk activity
Review lessons every fifth lesson, with script (cursive) reading practice

lessons.title: Lesson I: A Cat and a Rat
steps: New words: a, and, cat, rat; sound focus: short a; n, r, t, d
Read the lesson aloud together, pointing to each word; then let your child read it alone
Slate work: copy “a cat”
Sound out c-a-t and r-a-t with letter tiles or finger-taps, then swap the first letter to make new words (bat, hat)
questions: What two animals are in this lesson?
lessons.notes: First lesson: go slowly. Ten minutes of happy sounding-out beats a long, tired session.

lessons.title: Lesson II: Ann Has a Cat
steps: New words: at, the, ran, has, Ann; sound focus: h, th, s
You read a line, then your child reads it back; finish by reading the whole lesson together
Slate work: copy “The cat ran.”
Look at the picture and tell what the cat is doing
questions: Who has a cat?
What did the rat run at?

lessons.title: Lesson III: Ann and Nat
steps: New words: Nat, hat, fan, can; sound focus: f
Let your child read the lesson aloud slowly; help only on words they can't sound out
Slate work: copy “Ann has a fan.”
Make a paper fan together and act out the last sentence
questions: What does Ann have?
What does Nat have?

lessons.title: Lesson IV: The Man and the Lad
steps: New words: man, cap, lad, sat; sound focus: l, m, p, s
Read it once aloud for your child, then have them read it to you (or to a sibling or stuffed animal)
Slate work: copy “The lad has a cap.”
Tell back: who sat and who ran?
questions: Who sat, and who ran?
What does the lad have?
answers: The man sat; the lad ran

lessons.title: Lesson V: Review
steps: Read the lesson aloud together, pointing to each word; then let your child read it alone
Slate work: copy “The man has a hat.”
Read the script exercise together, matching script letters to print letters
questions: Who has a hat and a fan?
What does the man have?
lessons.notes: Review lesson: no new words. Let your child read it as independently as possible and note any words to revisit. This page has a script (cursive) exercise to read and copy.

lessons.title: Lesson VI: Rab the Dog
steps: New words: dog, Rab, fat, Nat's; sound focus: short o; b, g
You read a line, then your child reads it back; finish by reading the whole lesson together
Slate work: copy “a fat dog”
Talk about the picture: what is the dog looking at?
questions: What is the dog's name?
What does the dog have?

lessons.title: Lesson VII: The Frog on a Log
steps: New words: see, sees, frog, on, log; sound focus: long e (ee)
Let your child read the lesson aloud slowly; help only on words they can't sound out
Slate work: copy “See the frog on a log.”
Find all the words that rhyme with log (frog, dog)
questions: Where is the frog?
Who ran at the frog?

lessons.title: Lesson VIII: The Lamp
steps: New words: it, stand, Ann's, is, lamp, mat; sound focus: short i
Read it once aloud for your child, then have them read it to you (or to a sibling or stuffed animal)
Slate work: copy “The mat is on the stand.”
Narrate: where is the lamp, and what is under it?
questions: Where is the lamp?
Whose mat is it?
answers: On a mat on the stand

lessons.title: Lesson IX: Tom's Nag
steps: New words: Tom, nag, not, him, catch, he, his; sound focus: ch
Read the lesson aloud together, pointing to each word; then let your child read it alone
Slate work: copy “Can Tom catch his nag?”
Explain that a nag is a horse; let your child tell how the chase ended
questions: What is Tom trying to catch?
Can Tom catch it?

lessons.title: Lesson X: Review
steps: You read a line, then your child reads it back; finish by reading the whole lesson together
Slate work: copy “Tom sees Nat's dog.”
Pick three sentences and draw a picture for each
questions: Whose nag is fat?
Where did Ann sit?
lessons.notes: Review lesson: no new words. Let your child read it as independently as possible and note any words to revisit. This page has a script (cursive) exercise to read and copy.

lessons.title: Lesson XI: The Hen's Nest
steps: New words: nest, this, eggs, she, in, get, box, hen; sound focus: short e; x, sh
Let your child read the lesson aloud slowly; help only on words they can't sound out
Slate work: copy “She has eggs in the nest.”
Count real or toy eggs into a box as you reread the lesson
questions: Where is the hen's nest?
Who sees the nest?

lessons.title: Lesson XII: The Old Fox
steps: New words: old, run, fox; sound focus: long o; short u
Read it once aloud for your child, then have them read it to you (or to a sibling or stuffed animal)
Slate work: copy “This nest has eggs in it.”
Narrate: what does the fox want, and who is called to stop him?
questions: What does the fox want to catch?
Who is told to catch the fox?

lessons.title: Lesson XIII: Nell and the Ducks
steps: New words: pond, ducks, them, feed, Nell, I, by, will; sound focus: y as long i; w
Read the lesson aloud together, pointing to each word; then let your child read it alone
Slate work: copy “Nell will feed the ducks.”
Tell what you would feed ducks at a pond
questions: Where is Nell?
What will Nell do?

lessons.title: Lesson XIV: The Blind Man
steps: New words: holds, to, blind, Mary, hand, kind; sound focus: long i (kind, blind); long o (holds)
You read a line, then your child reads it back; finish by reading the whole lesson together
Slate work: copy “She is kind.”
Talk about one kind thing your child can do for someone today
questions: Why can't the old man see?
How does Mary help him?
answers: She holds him by the hand

lessons.title: Lesson XV: Review
steps: Let your child read the lesson aloud slowly; help only on words they can't sound out
Slate work: copy “Nell is kind to him.”
Retell the review in your own words: who is kind, and who gets the eggs?
questions: Who will get the eggs?
Who will feed the ducks?
lessons.notes: Review lesson: no new words. Let your child read it as independently as possible and note any words to revisit.

lessons.title: Lesson XVI: Sue's Doll
steps: New words: Sue, doll, dress, new, her, let; sound focus: ew
Read it once aloud for your child, then have them read it to you (or to a sibling or stuffed animal)
Slate work: copy “Sue has a doll.”
Play out the lesson with a doll or stuffed toy
questions: What is new on the doll?
Who gets to hold the doll?

lessons.title: Lesson XVII: The Bird's Nest
steps: New words: there, five, bird, tree, rob, do; sound focus: long i (five); v
Read the lesson aloud together, pointing to each word; then let your child read it alone
Slate work: copy “Do not rob the nest.”
Count to five on fingers for the eggs, then tell why we leave nests alone
questions: How many eggs are in the nest?
What should we not do?

lessons.title: Lesson XVIII: The Pet Bird
steps: New words: cage, pet, sing, lives, so, loves; sound focus: ng; soft g (cage)
You read a line, then your child reads it back; finish by reading the whole lesson together
Slate work: copy “It lives in a new cage.”
Narrate: tell three things about Sue's bird
questions: Where does the pet bird live?
What does the bird do on Sue's hand?

lessons.title: Lesson XIX: Boys at Play
steps: New words: are, you, yes, fast, too, like, boys, of, play; sound focus: oy; long a (play)
Let your child read the lesson aloud slowly; help only on words they can't sound out
Slate work: copy “I like to see boys play.”
Look at the snowy picture and name the games you see
questions: How many boys are playing?
Why can't Tom run fast?
Who can catch Tom?

lessons.title: Lesson XX: Review
steps: Read it once aloud for your child, then have them read it to you (or to a sibling or stuffed animal)
Slate work: copy “Sue has a new dress.”
Read the script exercise and copy one line
questions: What two things does Sue have?
Why won't Tom rob a nest?
answers: A doll and a pet bird
lessons.notes: Review lesson: no new words. Let your child read it as independently as possible and note any words to revisit. This page has a script (cursive) exercise to read and copy.

lessons.title: Lesson XXI: The Owl
steps: New words: what, night, owl, day, an, but, well, big, eyes, best; sound focus: ow; wh
Read the lesson aloud together, pointing to each word; then let your child read it alone
Slate work: copy “The owl can see best at night.”
Make big owl eyes with your fingers and say 'who, who' for each new word
questions: When can an owl see best?
Who has a pet owl?

lessons.title: Lesson XXII: Cows in the Shade
steps: New words: grass, they, come, off, barn, shade, hot, cows, out; sound focus: ou
You read a line, then your child reads it back; finish by reading the whole lesson together
Slate work: copy “They feed on the new grass.”
Narrate: where are the cows by day and by night?
questions: Where are the cows on the hot day?
Where do they go at night?
answers: In the shade of the big tree

lessons.title: Lesson XXIII: The Cow with a Bell
steps: New words: soon, sun, neck, set, way, bell, one, their; sound focus: oo
Let your child read the lesson aloud slowly; help only on words they can't sound out
Slate work: copy “The sun will soon set.”
Tell about the picture: what time of day is it?
questions: What does the old cow wear on her neck?
Where are the cows going?

lessons.title: Lesson XXIV: The Brave Men
steps: New words: brave, if, ship, boat, drown, men, rock, save; sound focus: long a (brave, save)
Read it once aloud for your child, then have them read it to you (or to a sibling or stuffed animal)
Slate work: copy “They will save the five men.”
Narrate the rescue in three sentences: what happened, who helped, how it ended
questions: What did the ship run onto?
How many men are on the ship?
Who will save them?
answers: The brave men in the boat

lessons.title: Lesson XXV: Review
steps: Read the lesson aloud together, pointing to each word; then let your child read it alone
Slate work: copy “The sun has set.”
Read one paragraph each, taking turns
questions: What bird has big eyes?
What do Ann and Nell like to do with their dolls?
answers: Rock them and sing to them
lessons.notes: Review lesson: no new words. Let your child read it as independently as possible and note any words to revisit.

lessons.title: Lesson XXVI: On the Ice
steps: New words: fall, ice, skates, cry, with, had, stone, did; sound focus: sk; aw sound in fall
You read a line, then your child reads it back; finish by reading the whole lesson together
Slate work: copy “He will not cry.”
Talk about a time your child fell and was brave
questions: Why did the boy fall?
Did he cry?
answers: He did not see the stone on the ice

lessons.title: Lesson XXVII: By the Mill
steps: New words: look, go, John, here, all, wheel, mill, have, round; sound focus: short oo (look); j
Let your child read the lesson aloud slowly; help only on words they can't sound out
Slate work: copy “The cows like grass.”
Explain what a mill wheel does; let your child spin a toy wheel as you reread
questions: Who is by the mill pond?
What do they like to watch?
lessons.notes: Includes a script exercise to copy.

lessons.title: Lesson XXVIII: Skates on the Floor
steps: New words: or, Jane, girls, floor, roll, some, which, black; sound focus: long o (roll); or
Read it once aloud for your child, then have them read it to you (or to a sibling or stuffed animal)
Slate work: copy “Their skates roll on the floor.”
Answer the question the lesson asks: ice or floor?
questions: Where are the girls skating?
Who wears the new black dress?

lessons.title: Lesson XXIX: Look Out for the Cars
steps: New words: for, out, as, how, try, horse, should, hurt, cars, be; sound focus: or; long e (be)
Read the lesson aloud together, pointing to each word; then let your child read it alone
Slate work: copy “How fast they come!”
Explain that 'the cars' means a train; talk about staying safe near tracks
questions: What can go faster than any horse?
Why won't the child try to catch the cars?
answers: He would fall and be hurt

lessons.title: Lesson XXX: Review
steps: You read a line, then your child reads it back; finish by reading the whole lesson together
Slate work: copy “How fast the cars go!”
Read the script exercise aloud, then copy it
questions: Why can't the mill wheel go round?
Who had a fall?
answers: There is ice on the pond
lessons.notes: Review lesson: no new words. Let your child read it as independently as possible and note any words to revisit. This page has a script (cursive) exercise to read and copy.

lessons.title: Lesson XXXI: Hard at Work
steps: New words: work, ax, pile, Ned, think, wood, saw, hard, cut; sound focus: th (think); or sound in work
Let your child read the lesson aloud slowly; help only on words they can't sound out
Slate work: copy “John has a saw.”
Answer the lesson's question: can they cut it all in one day?
questions: What tool does John have?
What tool does Ned have?

lessons.title: Lesson XXXII: A Walk in May
steps: New words: noise, air, hear, gone, May, walk, cool, two; sound focus: oi; long a (May)
Read it once aloud for your child, then have them read it to you (or to a sibling or stuffed animal)
Slate work: copy “Two girls have gone out for a walk.”
Take a short walk and listen, like the girls; name what you hear
questions: What month is it?
What two sounds do the girls hear?
answers: Birds singing and frogs in the pond

lessons.title: Lesson XXXIII: Bess and Her Goats
steps: New words: pull, cart, goats, Bess, up, ride, hill; sound focus: short u (up); u in pull
Read the lesson aloud together, pointing to each word; then let your child read it alone
Slate work: copy “She likes to ride in her cart.”
Narrate: why do the goats love Bess?
questions: What pulls Bess's cart?
Why do the goats love Bess?
answers: She feeds them and is kind to them

lessons.title: Lesson XXXIV: The House on Fire
steps: New words: blaze, put, yet, house, fire, roof, call, ring, we; sound focus: z
You read a line, then your child reads it back; finish by reading the whole lesson together
Slate work: copy “Run, boys, and ring the bell.”
Talk about what your family would do in a fire
questions: What part of the house is in a blaze?
What are the boys told to do?
answers: Ring the bell and call men to put out the fire

lessons.title: Lesson XXXV: Review: Tom and Bess
steps: Let your child read the lesson aloud slowly; help only on words they can't sound out
Slate work: copy “We can ride to the mill.”
Read it as a play: you are Tom, your child is Bess
questions: How are the logs cut at the mill?
How will Tom and Bess get to the mill?
lessons.notes: Review lesson: no new words. Let your child read it as independently as possible and note any words to revisit. Written as a conversation; it reads well with two voices.

lessons.title: Lesson XXXVI: Miss May's Rule
steps: New words: Miss, wants, would, tells, rule, keep, good, that, each; sound focus: long u (rule)
Read it once aloud for your child, then have them read it to you (or to a sibling or stuffed animal)
Slate work: copy “This is a good rule.”
Say the rule in your own words and give one example of keeping it
questions: Why do the children love Miss May?
What is the rule?
answers: She is so kind to them
Do to each one as you would like each one to do to you

lessons.title: Lesson XXXVII: The Schoolhouse
steps: New words: school, child, church, when, books, slates; sound focus: ch; oo (school)
Read the lesson aloud together, pointing to each word; then let your child read it alone
Slate work: copy “A good child likes to go to school.”
Look at the picture: what makes it look like a church?
questions: Is the building a church or a schoolhouse?
When will the children go in?

lessons.title: Lesson XXXVIII: The Quail
steps: New words: quail, quick, seen, kill, me, oh, eat, first, know, Henry; sound focus: qu
You read a line, then your child reads it back; finish by reading the whole lesson together
Slate work: copy “It is a quail.”
Read it with two voices, Henry and John
questions: What bird did Henry find?
Would John like to kill it?

lessons.title: Lesson XXXIX: Baby Kate
steps: New words: Kate, dear, name, blue, baby, near, shut, crib, sit; sound focus: long a (Kate, baby)
Let your child read the lesson aloud slowly; help only on words they can't sound out
Slate work: copy “Her name is Kate.”
Narrate: tell three things about Baby Kate
questions: What color are Kate's eyes?
Why can't you see her eyes?

lessons.title: Lesson XL: Review: Henry and Ned
steps: Read it once aloud for your child, then have them read it to you (or to a sibling or stuffed animal)
Slate work: copy “Her name is Kate.”
Compare Henry and Ned: who keeps the school rule?
questions: Who is first at school?
What did Ned try to do with a stone?
lessons.notes: Review lesson: no new words. Let your child read it as independently as possible and note any words to revisit. This page has a script (cursive) exercise to read and copy.

lessons.title: Lesson XLI: The Lighthouse
steps: New words: light, far, its, high, where, sea, tall, were; sound focus: igh
Read the lesson aloud together, pointing to each word; then let your child read it alone
Slate work: copy “The light is seen far out at sea.”
Answer the lesson's question: would you like to live in a lighthouse?
questions: Where does the lighthouse stand?
How does its light help the ships?
answers: On a high rock by the sea
Sailors can tell where to go and not run on the rocks

lessons.title: Lesson XLII: The Sheep and Lambs
steps: New words: wrong, wolf, us, my, took, sheep, more, watch, lambs; sound focus: wr; silent b (lambs)
You read a line, then your child reads it back; finish by reading the whole lesson together
Slate work: copy “Let us watch the sheep.”
Narrate: what happened to the other two lambs?
questions: What do the sheep like to eat?
What took two of the lambs?

lessons.title: Lesson XLIII: The Snow Man
steps: New words: laugh, snow, head, fun, mouth, made, pipe; sound focus: gh as f
Let your child read the lesson aloud slowly; help only on words they can't sound out
Slate work: copy “The boys have made a big snow man.”
Draw the snow man with his hat and pipe
questions: What is on the snow man's head?
What is in his mouth?

lessons.title: Lesson XLIV: The Bee and Mary
steps: New words: sweets, mean, please, bee, buzz, vine, could, said, once; sound focus: long e (bee, sweets); said and once are sight words
Read it once aloud for your child, then have them read it to you (or to a sibling or stuffed animal)
Slate work: copy “Buzz! buzz!”
Act it out: your child buzzes, you play Mary
questions: What did the bee say to Mary?
What did the bee want?

lessons.title: Lesson XLV: Review: By the Sea
steps: Read the lesson aloud together, pointing to each word; then let your child read it alone
Slate work: copy “What fun it is to see lambs play!”
Narrate the whole review story in order
questions: Where did Nat and the speaker sit?
What did the old wolf do once?
answers: On the high hill by the sea, near the lighthouse
Took a lamb and ran off with it
lessons.notes: Review lesson: no new words. Let your child read it as independently as possible and note any words to revisit.

units.title: Unit 10: Lessons XLVI–LII and Slate Exercises

lessons.title: Lesson XLVI: Work While You Work
steps: New words: while, might, time, things, done, right, your, halves; sound focus: long i (while, time, might)
You read a line, then your child reads it back; finish by reading the whole lesson together
Slate work: copy “Work while you work, play while you play.”
Memorize the first four lines together
questions: What should you do while you play?
Are things done by halves done right?
lessons.notes: The whole lesson is a script (cursive) poem; read it together and use it as copywork.

lessons.title: Lesson XLVII: John and Watch
steps: New words: went, fish, fell, safe, arms, sprang, was, thank, got; sound focus: sh; short e (went, fell)
Let your child read the lesson aloud slowly; help only on words they can't sound out
Slate work: copy “Thank you, my brave old dog.”
Narrate the story: what went wrong, and who saved John?
questions: What was John's dog named?
What happened when John got up to go?
answers: He fell off the log, and Watch sprang in to save him

lessons.title: Lesson XLVIII: James Drives On
steps: New words: James, asks, warm, town, then, drives, been, show; sound focus: ow (town, show)
Read it once aloud for your child, then have them read it to you (or to a sibling or stuffed animal)
Slate work: copy “James has been to the mill.”
Talk about how James was kind to his horse and to the girl
questions: Where has James been?
What did the girl ask him?
answers: To show her the way to the town

lessons.title: Lesson XLIX: My Dear Puss
steps: New words: I'll, she'll, don't, puss, pur, pat, fur, harm, deeds; sound focus: contractions (I'll, she'll, don't)
Read the lesson aloud together, pointing to each word; then let your child read it alone
Slate work: copy “I love my dear puss.”
Read the poem twice and clap the rhythm
questions: What will puss do when she is patted?
If you don't hurt her, what will she do?

lessons.title: Lesson L: Queen of the May
steps: New words: now, wreaths, who, queen, woods, shall, crown; sound focus: wr; qu
You read a line, then your child reads it back; finish by reading the whole lesson together
Slate work: copy “Who shall it be?”
Make a simple paper crown or flower wreath
questions: What day is it?
Who will be crowned Queen of the May?

lessons.title: Lesson LI: The Tall Tree
steps: New words: God, small, from, world, moon, shine, nut, long, ago; sound focus: all; long i (shine)
Let your child read the lesson aloud slowly; help only on words they can't sound out
Slate work: copy “God made the world.”
Find an acorn or seed outside and talk about how big it could grow
questions: What did the tall tree grow from?
What was made to shine at night?

lessons.title: Lesson LII: The Lord Is Near
steps: New words: Lord, smile, joys, tears, nigh, morn, griefs, woes, stars, say; sound focus: igh (nigh); oy (joys)
Read it once aloud for your child, then have them read it to you (or to a sibling or stuffed animal)
Slate work: copy “Think the Lord is near.”
Read the hymn slowly; explain nigh, morn, and woes
questions: When does the poem say the stars watch you?
What does the Lord see and hear?
answers: All you do and all you say

lessons.title: Slate Exercises and Script Alphabet
steps: Sound focus: spelling three-letter words letter by letter
Point to each letter of the slate words (nun, urn, sun, cow...) and blend them into the word
Slate work: copy “c a t  cat”
Trace the script alphabet and numbers 1 to 0 from the last page
questions: What word do the letters s-u-n spell?
What word do the letters h-e-n spell?
lessons.notes: This is the Primer's closing slate and script page, not a story. Spread it over a few days if your child is still learning to write.
